definition: Miscarriage is the spontaneous loss of a pregnancy before fetal viability, commonly before 20–24 weeks depending on local definition.
risks: Need for surgical evacuation if incomplete
treatment: Assess bleeding, pain, vital signs, and gestational age.
Confirm diagnosis with ultrasound and/or serial beta-hCG when available.
Provide expectant, medical, or surgical management depending on clinical status and patient preference.
Give anti-D immunoglobulin to Rh-negative women when indicated.
Provide pain relief, counselling, and follow-up care.
Treat infection urgently if suspected.

definition: Ectopic pregnancy occurs when a fertilized egg implants outside the uterine cavity, most commonly in the fallopian tube.
treatment: Assess vital signs and abdominal tenderness immediately.
Confirm with pregnancy test, ultrasound, and beta-hCG where available.
Stable patients may need methotrexate or surgical management depending on findings.
Unstable patients need emergency surgical management.
Arrange specialist obstetric or gynecological care.
urgent_referral_needed_if: Positive pregnancy test with severe abdominal pain

definition: Hyperemesis gravidarum is severe nausea and vomiting in pregnancy causing dehydration, weight loss, electrolyte imbalance, or ketonuria.
risks: Low birth weight if severe and prolonged
treatment: Assess hydration, weight loss, urine ketones, and electrolytes.
Advise small frequent meals and avoidance of triggers.
Give pregnancy-safe antiemetics according to local guideline.
Give oral or IV fluids depending on severity.
Give thiamine before glucose-containing IV fluids if prolonged vomiting.
Admit to hospital if severe dehydration or electrolyte abnormality is present.

definition: Septic abortion is infection of the uterus and surrounding tissues related to miscarriage or abortion.
treatment: Assess airway, breathing, circulation, vital signs, and sepsis signs.
Start broad-spectrum IV antibiotics urgently.
Give IV fluids and supportive care.
Remove retained products of conception after stabilization when indicated.
Monitor for shock and organ dysfunction.
Refer urgently for hospital management.

definition: Molar pregnancy is an abnormal pregnancy caused by abnormal trophoblastic tissue growth, also called hydatidiform mole.
treatment: Confirm with ultrasound and beta-hCG where available.
Refer for uterine evacuation by trained provider.
Monitor beta-hCG levels after evacuation until normal.
Avoid pregnancy during follow-up period as advised by specialist.
Treat complications such as bleeding or severe vomiting.

definition: Gestational hypertension is new-onset blood pressure ≥140/90 mmHg after 20 weeks of pregnancy without proteinuria or severe features.
treatment: Monitor blood pressure regularly.
Check urine protein and symptoms of pre-eclampsia.
Assess fetal growth and wellbeing.
Use antihypertensive treatment if severe hypertension or as locally recommended.
Plan timing of delivery based on gestational age, BP control, and maternal-fetal condition.
Refer if severe features develop.

definition: Pre-eclampsia is hypertension after 20 weeks of pregnancy with proteinuria and/or maternal organ dysfunction or uteroplacental dysfunction.
treatment: Assess blood pressure, urine protein, symptoms, and organ function.
Monitor platelets, liver enzymes, kidney function, and fetal wellbeing.
Use antihypertensives for severe hypertension.
Give magnesium sulfate if severe features or high seizure risk are present.
Plan delivery based on severity, gestational age, and maternal-fetal condition.
Refer for specialist obstetric care.
urgent_referral_needed_if: Epigastric or right upper abdominal pain

definition: Severe pre-eclampsia is pre-eclampsia with severe hypertension and/or signs of significant maternal organ dysfunction.
treatment: Admit or refer urgently for specialist care.
Stabilize airway, breathing, circulation, and blood pressure.
Start magnesium sulfate for seizure prevention according to protocol.
Treat severe hypertension with appropriate antihypertensive medicine.
Monitor urine output, reflexes, respiratory rate, and oxygen saturation.
Assess fetal wellbeing and plan delivery once mother is stabilized.

definition: Eclampsia is generalized tonic-clonic seizures during pregnancy or postpartum that cannot be explained by another neurological cause and is usually associated with pre-eclampsia.
treatment: Protect the patient from injury during seizures.
Maintain airway and place in left lateral position.
Give magnesium sulfate as first-line anticonvulsant treatment.
Continue magnesium sulfate for 24 hours after delivery or the last seizure, whichever is later.
Treat severe hypertension.
Monitor vital signs, reflexes, urine output, and fetal wellbeing.
Arrange delivery after maternal stabilization.
urgent_referral_needed_if: Any seizure during pregnancy or postpartum

definition: HELLP syndrome is a severe form of pre-eclampsia characterized by haemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, and low platelet count.
treatment: Refer urgently for hospital and specialist obstetric care.
Check complete blood count, platelets, liver enzymes, kidney function, and coagulation profile.
Stabilize blood pressure and maternal condition.
Give magnesium sulfate if pre-eclampsia/eclampsia risk is present.
Transfuse blood products if clinically indicated.
Plan delivery after stabilization depending on gestational age and severity.
urgent_referral_needed_if: Severe epigastric or right upper abdominal pain

definition: Gestational diabetes mellitus is glucose intolerance first recognized during pregnancy.
treatment: Screen using local antenatal diabetes testing protocol.
Advise healthy diet and safe physical activity.
Monitor blood glucose regularly.
Use insulin or other recommended therapy if glucose targets are not met.
Monitor fetal growth and amniotic fluid.
Plan delivery based on glucose control and fetal size.

definition: Iron deficiency anaemia in pregnancy occurs when iron deficiency causes low haemoglobin; anaemia is commonly defined as Hb below 11 g/dL in the first and third trimester and below 10.5 g/dL in the second trimester.
risks: Maternal heart failure in severe cases
treatment: Give oral iron and folic acid supplementation according to local guideline.
Advise iron-rich foods such as meat, fish, eggs, beans, lentils, and green leafy vegetables.
Avoid tea or coffee close to iron tablet intake.
Give vitamin C or vitamin C-rich foods to improve absorption.
Screen and treat causes such as hookworm or malaria where relevant.
Severe anaemia may require hospital management, IV iron, or blood transfusion.

definition: A urinary tract infection is a bacterial infection of the urinary tract during pregnancy, including asymptomatic bacteriuria and acute cystitis.
treatment: Perform urine dipstick and urine culture where available.
Treat with pregnancy-safe antibiotics according to local guideline and culture result.
Encourage adequate fluid intake.
Advise regular bladder emptying.
Review if symptoms do not improve within 48–72 hours.
Screen and treat asymptomatic bacteriuria where recommended.

definition: Pyelonephritis is an infection of the kidney during pregnancy and is usually considered a serious upper urinary tract infection.
treatment: Admit to hospital or refer urgently in most cases.
Start IV or IM pregnancy-safe antibiotics according to local guideline.
Give IV fluids if dehydrated.
Monitor temperature, blood pressure, urine output, and symptoms.
Send urine culture before antibiotics when possible.
Switch to oral antibiotics after clinical improvement to complete full course.

definition: Syphilis is a sexually transmitted bacterial infection caused by Treponema pallidum that can be transmitted to the fetus during pregnancy.
treatment: Use benzathine penicillin G as recommended treatment during pregnancy.
Treat according to syphilis stage and local guideline.
Evaluate and treat sexual partners.
Monitor for Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction after treatment.
Pregnant women with penicillin allergy should be referred for penicillin desensitization and penicillin treatment.
Arrange follow-up serology.

definition: Gonorrhoea is a sexually transmitted bacterial infection caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae that may affect the mother and newborn.
treatment: Treat with pregnancy-safe antibiotic regimen according to current local guideline.
Evaluate for chlamydia and other sexually transmitted infections.
Treat sexual partners to prevent reinfection.
Advise abstinence from sexual activity until treatment is completed and partners are treated.
Arrange follow-up testing when indicated.

definition: Chorioamnionitis is infection and inflammation of the fetal membranes and amniotic fluid, usually occurring during labour or after membrane rupture.
treatment: Refer urgently for hospital obstetric management.
Start broad-spectrum IV antibiotics according to local guideline.
Monitor maternal vital signs and fetal heart rate.
Plan delivery based on maternal and fetal condition.
Provide fluids, antipyretics, and supportive care.
Assess newborn for infection after delivery.

definition: Malaria in pregnancy is infection with Plasmodium parasites during pregnancy and can cause severe maternal and fetal complications.
treatment: Test for malaria promptly in endemic areas.
Treat confirmed malaria with pregnancy-appropriate antimalarial therapy according to trimester and local guideline.
Give antipyretics and fluids as needed.
Assess and treat anaemia.
Severe malaria requires urgent hospital management with parenteral antimalarial therapy.
Use preventive measures in endemic areas.

definition: Polyhydramnios is excessive accumulation of amniotic fluid during pregnancy, commonly diagnosed by ultrasound.
treatment: Monitor maternal condition and fetal wellbeing closely.
Perform ultrasound assessment of amniotic fluid volume and fetal anatomy.
Screen for gestational diabetes.
Assess for multiple pregnancy and fetal abnormalities.
Monitor for preterm labour.
Provide supportive care for discomfort and breathing difficulty.
Refer for specialist obstetric assessment if moderate or severe.

definition: Oligohydramnios is reduced amniotic fluid volume during pregnancy, usually diagnosed by ultrasound.
risks: Pulmonary hypoplasia if very early and severe
treatment: Confirm by ultrasound and assess fetal growth.
Evaluate for ruptured membranes, placental insufficiency, and fetal anomalies.
Monitor fetal wellbeing closely.
Encourage adequate maternal hydration where appropriate.
Plan timing of delivery depending on gestational age and fetal condition.
Refer for specialist obstetric care.

definition: Placenta previa occurs when the placenta partly or completely covers the internal cervical opening after mid-pregnancy.
symptoms: Painless vaginal bleeding in second or third trimester
treatment: Confirm placental location with ultrasound.
Avoid digital vaginal examination until placenta previa is excluded.
Monitor bleeding, maternal vitals, and fetal wellbeing.
Give anti-D to Rh-negative women when indicated.
Hospitalize or refer if bleeding occurs.
Plan delivery mode and timing with specialist obstetric team.

definition: Placental abruption is premature separation of the placenta from the uterine wall before delivery.
treatment: Treat as obstetric emergency.
Assess vital signs, bleeding, abdominal tenderness, and fetal heart rate.
Start IV access, fluids, blood tests, and crossmatch where available.
Monitor for coagulopathy.
Plan urgent delivery depending on maternal and fetal condition.
Refer urgently to hospital.

definition: Placenta accreta spectrum is abnormal adherence or invasion of the placenta into the uterine wall.
symptoms: Failure of placenta to separate after delivery
treatment: Identify risk factors such as previous caesarean and placenta previa.
Diagnose using ultrasound and specialist imaging when needed.
Plan delivery in a facility with blood bank and experienced surgical team.
Avoid manual removal if accreta is strongly suspected.
Prepare for haemorrhage management and possible hysterectomy.
Provide multidisciplinary specialist care.

definition: Fetal growth restriction is when a fetus does not reach its expected growth potential, often due to placental, maternal, or fetal causes.
treatment: Confirm fetal size and growth with ultrasound.
Assess amniotic fluid and Doppler studies where available.
Identify and manage maternal causes such as hypertension or smoking.
Monitor fetal movement and fetal wellbeing.
Plan delivery timing based on gestational age and fetal condition.
Refer for specialist obstetric care.

definition: Fetal distress refers to signs that the fetus may not be receiving adequate oxygen, commonly suspected from abnormal fetal heart rate or reduced fetal movement.
severe_symptoms: Severe meconium with abnormal heart rate
treatment: Assess fetal heart rate and maternal condition immediately.
Place mother in left lateral position and correct maternal hypotension if present.
Give oxygen only if clinically indicated by maternal condition.
Stop uterotonic infusion if excessive contractions occur.
Treat underlying cause where possible.
Arrange urgent obstetric review and delivery if distress persists.
urgent_referral_needed_if: Absent or markedly reduced fetal movement
Meconium with abnormal fetal heart rate

definition: Intrauterine fetal death is death of the fetus before birth after the gestational age considered fetal viability or stillbirth threshold by local definition.
symptoms: Uterus may measure small for dates
treatment: Confirm diagnosis by ultrasound.
Provide sensitive counselling and emotional support.
Investigate possible causes where appropriate.
Plan induction or delivery according to gestational age, maternal condition, and patient preference.
Monitor for infection, bleeding, and coagulopathy when indicated.
Offer bereavement support and follow-up.

definition: Preterm labour is regular uterine contractions with cervical change before 37 completed weeks of pregnancy.
treatment: Assess gestational age, contractions, cervical change, membranes, and fetal wellbeing.
Refer for obstetric assessment.
Give antenatal corticosteroids when indicated for fetal lung maturity.
Use tocolysis when appropriate and not contraindicated.
Give magnesium sulfate for fetal neuroprotection when indicated by gestational age.
Treat infection if present.

definition: PROM is rupture of fetal membranes before onset of labour at or after 37 weeks of pregnancy.
symptoms: Sudden gush of fluid from vagina
treatment: Confirm rupture of membranes and assess fetal wellbeing.
Avoid unnecessary digital vaginal examinations.
Monitor temperature, pulse, uterine tenderness, and fetal heart rate.
Manage according to gestational age and infection risk.
Use antibiotics if infection is suspected or according to local protocol.
Plan induction or delivery according to guideline.

definition: PPROM is rupture of fetal membranes before onset of labour and before 37 completed weeks of pregnancy.
treatment: Refer for hospital obstetric assessment.
Confirm membrane rupture and assess gestational age.
Avoid digital vaginal examination unless delivery is imminent.
Monitor for infection and fetal wellbeing.
Give antibiotics and antenatal corticosteroids when indicated.
Give magnesium sulfate for fetal neuroprotection when indicated.
Plan timing of delivery based on gestational age and infection or fetal risk.

definition: Malpresentation occurs when the fetus is not in a normal head-first position near term, such as breech or transverse lie.
symptoms: Abnormal fetal position on abdominal examination
Hard fetal head felt in upper uterus
severe_symptoms: Ruptured membranes with high presenting part
treatment: Confirm presentation by clinical examination and ultrasound.
Assess gestational age and fetal condition.
Consider external cephalic version near term when appropriate and no contraindication.
Plan safe mode of delivery based on presentation, parity, fetal size, and facility capability.
Refer for specialist obstetric care if persistent malpresentation.
urgent_referral_needed_if: Labour with breech presentation where skilled care unavailable

definition: Cord prolapse occurs when the umbilical cord descends through the cervix beside or before the presenting fetal part after membrane rupture.
symptoms: Sudden fetal heart rate abnormality after membrane rupture
severe_symptoms: Maternal panic or emergency labour situation
treatment: Call for emergency obstetric help immediately.
Avoid handling the cord excessively.
Relieve cord compression by elevating presenting part manually if trained.
Place mother in knee-chest or left lateral head-down position while preparing delivery.
Keep exposed cord moist with sterile saline gauze if visible.
Arrange immediate delivery, usually emergency caesarean unless vaginal birth is imminent.
urgent_referral_needed_if: Sudden fetal bradycardia after membrane rupture
Ruptured membranes with high presenting part

definition: Obstructed labour occurs when the fetus cannot progress through the birth canal despite strong uterine contractions.
treatment: Recognize prolonged labour early using partograph or labour monitoring.
Assess maternal vital signs, contractions, fetal heart rate, and labour progress.
Do not continue labour if obstruction is suspected.
Give IV fluids and antibiotics if infection suspected.
Arrange urgent operative delivery by skilled team.
Refer urgently to comprehensive emergency obstetric care.
urgent_referral_needed_if: No progress in labour despite strong contractions

definition: Uterine rupture is tearing of the uterine wall during pregnancy or labour, more common in women with previous uterine surgery.
treatment: Treat as life-threatening obstetric emergency.
Resuscitate with IV fluids, blood products, and oxygen as needed.
Arrange immediate laparotomy and delivery.
Monitor maternal vital signs and fetal condition.
Prepare for uterine repair or hysterectomy depending on injury and bleeding.
Refer to emergency obstetric surgical facility immediately.
urgent_referral_needed_if: Sudden severe abdominal pain in labour
Previous caesarean with labour pain and bleeding

definition: Shoulder dystocia is an obstetric emergency where the fetal shoulders fail to deliver after the head due to impaction behind the maternal pelvis.
treatment: Call for help immediately.
Avoid excessive traction on fetal head.
Use McRoberts manoeuvre and suprapubic pressure first.
Proceed to internal manoeuvres if needed by trained provider.
Prepare for neonatal resuscitation.
Document timing, manoeuvres, and outcome.
urgent_referral_needed_if: Shoulders not delivered after fetal head

definition: Postpartum haemorrhage is excessive bleeding after birth, commonly defined as blood loss of 500 mL or more after vaginal birth or 1000 mL or more after caesarean birth, or any bleeding causing instability.
treatment: Call for help and assess airway, breathing, and circulation.
Massage uterus and give uterotonic medicine according to protocol.
Establish IV access and give fluids or blood products as needed.
Identify cause using tone, trauma, tissue, and thrombin approach.
Remove retained tissue and repair trauma when indicated.
Refer urgently if bleeding continues or surgical care is needed.
urgent_referral_needed_if: Bleeding not responding to uterine massage and uterotonics

definition: Retained placenta occurs when the placenta is not delivered within the expected time after birth or when placental tissue remains inside the uterus.
symptoms: Uterus may be enlarged or soft
risks: Need for manual removal or surgery
treatment: Assess bleeding and maternal vital signs.
Give uterotonic medicines as indicated.
Do controlled cord traction only by trained provider when appropriate.
Do not pull forcefully on cord.
Manual removal under appropriate analgesia/anaesthesia may be required.
Give antibiotics according to local protocol if manual removal or infection risk.
Refer urgently if bleeding or placenta remains retained.

definition: Puerperal sepsis is infection of the genital tract occurring after delivery or miscarriage, usually within 42 days postpartum.
treatment: Assess vital signs and signs of sepsis urgently.
Start broad-spectrum antibiotics according to local guideline.
Give IV fluids and supportive care if unwell.
Evaluate for retained products, endometritis, wound infection, or abscess.
Remove retained products if present after stabilization.
Refer urgently for hospital management if severe.
urgent_referral_needed_if: Fever after birth with foul-smelling lochia

definition: Postpartum endometritis is infection of the uterine lining after childbirth, more common after caesarean delivery or prolonged rupture of membranes.
treatment: Assess postpartum fever and uterine tenderness.
Start broad-spectrum antibiotics according to local guideline.
Monitor temperature, pulse, pain, and lochia.
Evaluate for retained products or wound infection if not improving.
Provide fluids, analgesia, and supportive care.
Refer if severe or persistent infection.

definition: Mastitis is inflammation or infection of breast tissue during breastfeeding, often associated with milk stasis.
treatment: Continue breastfeeding or milk expression unless advised otherwise.
Ensure proper latch and frequent milk drainage.
Use warm compresses before feeding and analgesics as appropriate.
Give antibiotics if bacterial mastitis is suspected or symptoms are severe/persistent.
Assess for abscess if localized swelling or no improvement.
Encourage rest and fluids.

definition: Postpartum depression is a depressive disorder occurring after childbirth that causes persistent low mood, loss of interest, and impaired functioning.
severe_symptoms: Inability to care for self or baby
treatment: Screen with a validated tool such as EPDS or PHQ-9 where available.
Provide supportive counselling and involve family support when safe.
Offer psychological therapy for mild to moderate cases.
Consider antidepressant treatment when indicated by a qualified clinician.
Create a safety plan if self-harm thoughts are present.
Refer urgently for severe depression or safety concerns.
urgent_referral_needed_if: Neglect of baby due to illness

definition: Postpartum psychosis is a rare but severe psychiatric emergency after childbirth involving psychosis, mood disturbance, and impaired reality testing.
severe_symptoms: Thoughts of harming self or baby
treatment: Treat as psychiatric emergency.
Ensure mother and baby safety immediately.
Arrange urgent mental health specialist assessment.
Hospital admission is usually required.
Medication such as antipsychotics or mood stabilizers may be needed under specialist care.
Involve trusted family or caregivers for supervision and support.
